name: Shopify
flow: free trial start to first product added

steps.title: Shopify: The All-in-One Commerce Platform for Businesses - Shopify
steps.note: Next: clicked "Get started fast You could be selling by tomorrow."

steps.title: Start your online store today. Start selling tomorrow. - Shopify
steps.note: Stopped: account form or bot check reached.

jtbd_fit.evidence: Hero says "Dream big and build fast on Shopify. The world's best commerce platform." Names commerce but not the merchant's job.

capability_visible.evidence: Step 1 hero is a dark lifestyle video with no product UI.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Not visible in captured steps; "Pricing" sits in nav only.

time_to_value.evidence: Flow stopped before account creation; cannot judge.

friction.evidence: The hero "Start for free" leads to /start, a second page with the same CTA again (step 2). One extra click for the same intent.

trust.evidence: No trust signals in the captured viewport.

mobile.evidence: Mobile capture exists for step 1 but was not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: Headline "Be the next AI all-star" does not say what a merchant gets; the clear line is the subhead.

proof_quality.evidence: "The world's best commerce platform" is stated with no evidence on the screen.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: No fake urgency or pressure visible; the promise is speed ("Be selling by tomorrow").

cta_logic.evidence: One consistent label, "Start for free", in nav and hero, but it is repeated on an interstitial.

read.summary: A confident, brand-led landing that asks for the click before showing the product. The path to signup is consistent in wording but takes an extra interstitial.
pros: One CTA wording everywhere ("Start for free") keeps the decision simple.
"Be selling by tomorrow" is a concrete, merchant-relevant speed promise.
No visible urgency or pressure tactics in these steps.
cons: Hero headline is about AI ambition rather than the merchant's job.
No product UI or proof on the first screen.
The /start page re-asks for the same click.
read.howItSells: Sells identity and momentum ("be the next all-star", "start today") with a low-commitment free start. Relies on brand authority more than shown evidence.
copy: Speed-framed promise next to a single, repeated CTA.
avoid: Leading with an abstract headline and holding back the product.
An interstitial that repeats the CTA.
unknowns: What the real account form asks for.
Whether /start varies by visitor or campaign.

hypothesis.statement: Showing a short product demo above the fold will lift hero-to-signup click rate without hurting signup completion.
hypothesis.metric: Hero CTA click-through to account-created rate
hypothesis.guardrail: Page load time and bounce rate
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if CTA-to-account rises with no guardrail regression after a two-week split test.
